# shadow/signal-must-be-called

Require signal and memo accessors to be called when a value is needed.

`recommended` `fixable` `has suggestions` `uses types when available`

## Why

`useSignal` and `useMemo` return functions. In JSX children and attributes the runtime accepts the bare accessor (`{count}`), but in arithmetic, comparisons, conditions, template strings and member access a function is not the value: `count + 1` is a string, `if (count)` is always true and `count.length` is the function's arity. Call the accessor.

## Incorrect

```tsx
const [count, setCount] = useSignal(0);
const next = count + 1;
```

```tsx
const [items] = useSignal<string[]>([]);
const size = items.length;
```

```tsx
const [count] = useSignal(0);
const label = `Count: ${count}`;
```

```tsx
const [count] = useSignal(0);
if (count) { start(); }
```

## Correct

```tsx
const [count, setCount] = useSignal(0);
const next = count() + 1;
```

```tsx
const [count] = useSignal(0);
const view = <span>{count}</span>;
```

```tsx
const [state] = useStore({ n: 0 });
const next = state.n + 1;
```

## Autofix and suggestions

An accessor declared by a ShadowJS hook (`useSignal`, `useMemo`, `useResource`, `useSelector`, `children`, a primitive `useStore`) is fixed by inserting `()` after it. An identifier found only through type information (a zero-argument function type) gets a suggestion to call it instead, because calling an arbitrary function is not known to be safe.

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/signal-must-be-called`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/signal-must-be-called */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/signal-must-be-called */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. When the function itself is the intended value, for example reading a property of the function (`handler.name`) or printing its source text on purpose.

## Notes

- Accessors are found from `useSignal`, `useMemo`, `useResource`, `useSelector` and `children` declarations and their aliases.
- With a type-aware parser (`parserOptions.projectService`), zero-argument function types are also reported, as suggestions.
- Members the accessor really has are not reported: a resource's `state`, `loading`, `error`, `latest`, `refetch`, `mutate`, and `children().toArray()`.

## Messages

- `mustCall`: `{{name}}` is a {{kind}} accessor: call it (`{{name}}()`) to read the value here.
- `mustCallTyped`: `{{name}}` is a function that returns a value: call it (`{{name}}()`) here.
- `callIt`: Call `{{name}}()`.
